description: Adds a new container (group/swimlane) to a live Trident document. Containers visually group related nodes. Use get_document_summary to check existing container IDs before adding to avoid duplicates. Requires a valid editor access token. To build an ERD (entity-relationship diagram), add one container per table with kind:"erd" and an x/y position, then add each field with add_node (container:<table id>, no x/y) — rows are stacked and the table sized automatically — and join TABLES (never rows) with add_connection using an ERD pair type such as "one_to_many".

action_explanation.description: Optional: brief explanation of what this action does and why (max 250 chars). Shown live to human collaborators in the AI cursor tooltip.

agentId.description: YOUR AI assistant name (e.g. "Claude.ai", "GitHub Copilot"). Shown as "[agentId] working with [userName]" in the collaboration presence dot.

color.description: Optional: background color (hex or color name)

height.description: Optional: fixed height (use with width). Not for ERD tables. If you give a container a fixed size, make sure every node you add to it fits inside, or enlarge it with update_container.

id.description: Unique ID for the container (no spaces)

kind.description: Optional: "erd" makes this container an ERD table (flat table: the label is the table name, child nodes are its field rows). Omit for a regular container.

label.description: Display label for the container header

outlineColor.description: Optional: border/outline color (hex or color name), e.g. "#5B7A99" for a C4 system boundary.

width.description: Optional: fixed width. Omit width/height to let the container auto-size around its nodes. ERD tables default to 220; their height is managed automatically (28 header + 24 per row), so do not set it.

x.description: Optional: X position (required for kind:"erd" — the centre of the table)

y.description: Optional: Y position (required for kind:"erd" — the centre of the table)

token.description: Editor access token for this document. The document ID is embedded in the token.

userName.description: First name of the human you are assisting (ask them at session start if you do not know). Shown in the collaboration presence dot as "[agentId] working with [userName]".

name: add_container
